newsitem.title: USA: Reuter poll shows Dole in post-debate gain.
newsitem.headline: Reuter poll shows Dole in post-debate gain.

text.p: Republican Bob Dole closed the gap in his race with President Bill Clinton for a second straight day following the Wednesday presidential debate, according to the daily Reuters tracking poll on Saturday.
Dole got 36.8 percent in the John Zogby Group International poll, up from 34.6, against 44.6 for Clinton, up from 43.6.
The poll of 900 likely voters, with a 3.3 percent margin of error, showed support for independent candidate Ross Perot fell to 5.1 percent from 5.8.

Zogby said the Sunday poll would likely see further Dole gains because they reflected a rolling average of three days, and Wednesday's results were low while the post-debate results on Thursday and Friday rose.
But the poll-taker added that while Dole increased his margin after the first debate, it later fell off.
Zogby said the Saturday poll showed Dole winning support from his Republican base, but he has not broken new ground.
He said Dole has not won over political moderates or got new support among white men. "What we're seeing here is the result of Republicans coming back home. But that is not going to be enough."

Zogby said if Sunday's figures showed another Dole increase, "we are looking at a tightening of the race. But the magic number for Dole is 40 percent. He has failed to reach that number in our poll or anyone's."

In House races, the poll showed Republicans ahead 41.5 percent to 37.5, a drop from Friday's showing of 39.5 to 38.7, and in the Senate, the Republicans led by 42.7 to 37.4, against 41.1 to 37.9 on Friday.
Zogby said Republicans are now seemingly safe in both the Senate and House, but if Clinton widens his lead, that could change.
"Our rule is that if Clinton is ahead by 10 points," he said, "the Democrats take the House and if there is a 13 point lead, the Democrats take the Senate," margins Clinton does not now hold.
